message.content:
1. Use LC‑MS‑grade water, methanol, isopropanol, acetic acid and formic acid (all from Merck) for all solutions.  
2. Prepare methanolic working solutions of cortisol (CORT), cortisone (CORN) and the isotopically‑labelled internal standards CORT‑D₄ and CORN‑D₈ (15 ng mL⁻¹ each) and store at –20 °C until use.  
3. For each hair sample (≈35 mg dry weight) do the following pretreatment:  
   a. Place the hair in a tube, add 5 mL isopropanol, shake manually for 3 min, discard the liquid; repeat twice with fresh isopropanol.  
   b. Dry the hair overnight at room temperature, then cut into ~2 mm pieces with surgical scissors.  
   c. Weigh 35 mg of the cut hair into a 15 mL Falcon tube.  
   d. Homogenise with five 2 mm steel balls in a Bioprep‑24R Homogeniser (5 × 30 s cycles, 10 °C, with cooling intervals).  

4. Extraction for UHPLC‑ESI‑MS/MS:  
   a. Add 1 mL methanol containing the internal standards (CORT‑D₄ and CORN‑D₈, 15 ng mL⁻¹) to the powdered hair.  
   b. Incubate 24 h on a SSL4 see‑saw rocker (70 rpm, room temperature).  
   c. Centrifuge 10 min at 13 000 rpm (Eppendorf 5415R).  
   d. Transfer 800 µL supernatant to a new tube and evaporate to dryness in a Genevac EZ‑2 Elite evaporator.  
   e. Re‑constitute the residue in 1 mL LC‑MS‑grade water, sonicate 2 min.  

5. Solid‑phase extraction (SPE):  
   a. Use a Gilson GX‑271 ASPEC system with Strata‑X 30 mg cartridges (p/n 8B‑S100‑TAK).  
   b. Condition each cartridge with 1 mL methanol, equilibrate with 1 mL water.  
   c. Load the 1 mL reconstituted extract onto the cartridge, wash with 1 mL water, elute with 1 mL methanol.  
   d. Concentrate the eluate to 200 µL, transfer to a glass chromatography vial.  

6. UHPLC‑ESI‑MS/MS analysis:  
   a. Instrument: Agilent 1290 Infinity UHPLC + Agilent 6460 triple‑quadrupole (Jet Stream ESI).  
   b. Column: Waters BEH C18, 1.7 µm, 2.1 × 100 mm, maintained at 40 °C.  
   c. Mobile phase A = 0.1 % formic acid in water; mobile phase B = methanol.  
   d. Flow = 0.2 mL min⁻¹; gradient: 0‑4 min 20 %→60 % B, 4‑5 min 60 % B, 5‑7 min 60 %→70 % B, 7‑9 min 70 % B, post‑run 2 min.  
   e. Injection volume = 5 µL.  
   f. Acquire in dMRM mode, positive ionisation; use the following transitions (precursor → product, fragmentor V, collision eV, RT min):  
      - CORN 361.1 → 163 (160 V, 24 eV, 6.3 ± 0.4) and 361.1 → 121 (160 V, 36 eV).  
      - CORN‑D₈ 369.1 → 169.1 (160 V, 30 eV, 6.3 ± 0.4).  
      - CORT 363 → 121.2 (80 V, 26 eV, 6.8 ± 0.4) and 363 → 97.5 (80 V, 36 eV).  
      - CORT‑D₄ 367.1 → 121.1 (80 V, 26 eV, 6.8 ± 0.4).  
   g. Source settings: nebuliser 35 psi, drying gas 300 °C at 8 L min⁻¹, sheath gas 300 °C at 10 L min⁻¹, capillary 4500 V, nozzle 300 V.  

7. ELISA (for nine selected samples):  
   a. Weigh 35 mg of powdered hair into a tube, add 1.8 mL methanol, vortex, incubate overnight on an orbital shaker.  
   b. Centrifuge, evaporate the supernatant to dryness under nitrogen at 37 °C.  
   c. Re‑constitute in 400 µL ELISA buffer (Cayman Chemical Cortisol ELISA Kit, cat. 500360).  
   d. Follow the manufacturer’s protocol for assay setup, washing (ELx50 plate washer), incubation (ELMI DTS‑4 shaker) and detection (Synergy 2 plate reader, 410 nm).  
   e. Convert the calibration curve results from pg mL⁻¹ to pg mg⁻¹ hair using the re‑constitution volume and the original hair mass.  

8. Provide us with the raw LC‑MS/MS data (chromatograms, peak areas), the calculated concentrations (ng mg⁻¹ hair), and the ELISA results for the nine comparison samples.  

Please let us know if any of the required reagents, consumables (Strata‑X cartridges, internal standards) or equipment (Bioprep‑24R, Gilson GX‑271, Agilent 6460) are unavailable, and we will arrange alternatives. Thanks.
